normalized.governing_thought: Yes, raise prices in 2027, but not 12% on every plan: price mid-market and enterprise now, and hold SMB until the evidence is in
executive_summary: Churn is a cohort problem, not a market-wide price problem

SMB monthly churn rose 2.0% → 3.1%; ~90% of the rise comes from the 2,100 customers who joined on the 2025 50%-off promotion. Other SMB customers churn at 2.1% (2.0% a year ago) and only 18% of them cite price (19% in 2025). Mid-market 0.6% → 0.8%; enterprise flat at 0.2%.
The headroom is in mid-market and enterprise

76% of ARR, net revenue retention (NRR) of 112% and 118%; customers stay for integrations and the audit trail; a +10% price test showed no significant conversion loss. SMB is where Inkwell's $9 plan is winning: win rate 51% → 38%.
Only $7.6M can be repriced in 2027 (15% of mid-market and 60% of enterprise ARR do not renew; enterprise caps at 7%). After the likely churn response it is $4.5–6.3M.

Mid-market +10% at renewal; enterprise at contract terms (7% where capped, 10% otherwise): +$4.3M. SMB list price held through June while a controlled +8% test runs; go or no-go for the second half (+$0.4M). Activation programme for the promotion cohort (+$0.3M). ≈ $98.9M exit ARR, exactly the +15% target, before any new-customer ARR; NRR ≈ 115%.

≈ $1.6M less 2027 ARR than the CFO plan's base case on paper. In exchange: no wider price gap against Inkwell where Palisade is losing deals, and a measured answer on SMB price sensitivity before 5,900 customers are committed to it.
Decisions needed in December: approve mid-market and enterprise renewal pricing · hold SMB and approve the test and June gate · fund the activation programme · restate the board churn metric

slides.title: Churn rose almost only in SMB; mid-market edged up and enterprise is flat

evidence: Cohort churn implied from mid-2026 counts: (5,900 × 3.1% − 3,800 × 2.1%) ÷ 2,100 = 4.9%. Mix effect = 3.1% − 2.1%.

evidence: ~4.9% implied monthly churn, vs 2.1% for other SMB customers

evidence: Churned SMB customers whose main exit reason was “price / found a cheaper option”: All SMB churners, H1 2025: 19%

claims.claim: Inkwell is winning new SMB business on price
evidence: 51% → 38% Palisade's SMB win rate when Inkwell was considered, H1 2025 → H1 2026
List price per user per month: Inkwell Starter (Oct 2025) $9; Palisade SMB $15; Palisade SMB at +12% $16.80; Inkwell Pro $24; Palisade Business $29

claims.claim: A 12% rise takes the SMB plan from 1.7× to 1.9× Inkwell Starter. Inkwell has not been seen in mid-market or enterprise deals above 200 seats.

slides.title: The CFO's $10.3M assumes all ARR reprices in 2027; renewal timing and contract caps cut it to $7.6M, and churn to $4.5–6.3M

claims.claim: ARR gained from +12% on every plan in 2027, $M (waterfall)
Renewal timing. Price changes apply at renewal; 85% of mid-market and 40% of enterprise ARR renew in 2027.
Contract caps. 60% of enterprise ARR cannot rise more than 7% a year.
SMB churn. In 2023, +8% raised SMB churn by 0.5 pts for six months and 0.1 pts after; scaled to 12% that loses ~5% of SMB ARR.
Not counted: any loss of new SMB deals to Inkwell from a higher list price.
SMB is the weak link: of its $2.5M gross gain, $1.3M (base) to $2.5M (downside) goes back out as churn.

slides.title: Of three options, a segmented increase meets the 15% growth target with the least exposure in SMB

claims.claim: A · CFO plan: +12% on every plan — NOT RECOMMENDED
evidence: Price moves: +12% at renewal on all plans and list prices from January
SMB exposure: All 5,900 SMB customers, plus new buyers at $16.80 vs Inkwell's $9
Main risk: SMB deals and promotion-cohort churn; 2027 churn signal becomes hard to read

claims.claim: B · Hold prices, fix onboarding — NOT RECOMMENDED
evidence: Main risk: Misses the target unless new-customer ARR is ≥ $4.7M; leaves mid-market and enterprise headroom unused

claims.claim: C · Segmented increase (recommended) — RECOMMENDED
evidence: Price moves: Mid-market +10%, enterprise at terms from January; SMB +8% from July only if the test passes
SMB exposure: None until July; +8% for the core base only if the test passes; promotion cohort deferred to 2028
Main risk: ≈ $1.6M below A in the base case; downside needs ≥ $1.1M of new-customer ARR

claims.claim: All options include promotion-cohort activation (+$0.3M).
evidence: Base = $86.0M × each segment's trailing NRR = $94.0M. Downside = stronger churn response, no activation gain, SMB test fails.

slides.title: The recommended plan reaches the +15% target ($98.9M) before any new-customer ARR, but with no margin to spare

claims.claim: Exit-2027 ARR, base case, $M (bridge)
Downside: $97.8M. Mid-market reacts at renewal, activation gains nothing, the SMB test fails. Closing the gap needs ≥ $1.1M of new-customer ARR.
New-customer ARR is the buffer. It is not in the pack; Sales should confirm the 2027 plan before the board meeting.
Spare lever: if mid-market renewals hold through June, renew the second half at +12% (+$0.35M).
Timing: each month of renewals missed because notice periods have passed costs ≈ $0.36M.

slides.title: Against the CFO plan we give up ≈ $1.6M of 2027 ARR on paper: about half from deferring SMB, half from staying at the tested 10% in mid-market

claims.claim: Where the $1.6M gap comes from (base case, $M)
evidence: SMB +12% in January, net of churn: 1.25
Mid-market and enterprise at 12% instead of 10%: +0.77

claims.claim: An answer to the biggest open question. How price-sensitive the core SMB base is now that Inkwell exists, measured before committing all 5,900 customers.
No wider gap at the point of sale. SMB win rate against Inkwell is already down 13 points; neither A nor C counts the effect on new deals.
A clean read on onboarding. With SMB prices unchanged, 2027 churn shows whether activation works.
Mid-market stays at the tested level on 48% of ARR. The test covered new sign-ups, not renewals.
Where the CFO is right: the churn rise is mostly an onboarding and cohort problem. That is why mid-market and enterprise go ahead in January.
In the downside case the January SMB rise nets ≈ $0: $2.5M of extra churn cancels $2.5M of price. Deferring it costs at most ≈ $0.85M.

slides.title: Onboarding will help, but it cannot halve SMB churn in two quarters: low activation explains under a third of the cohort's excess churn

claims.claim: Promotion-cohort monthly churn split into its drivers, H1 2026 (%)
evidence: The activation share applies the pack's “~3× churn below five documents” to each cohort's activation mix.

claims.claim: SMB monthly churn under different outcomes
evidence: Lowest SMB rate in the pack (pre-2023): 1.8%

slides.title: How: mid-market and enterprise renewals start in January, SMB is tested in the first half, and leadership decides in June

claims.claim: Mid-market and enterprise pricing: Notices (Dec); Mid-market +10% and enterprise at terms, applied at each renewal. Owner: CFO + Sales
SMB price test: Design; +8% test: new sign-ups and a 10% sample of renewals; If go: +8% list; core base at renewal. Owner: Growth / Product
Promotion-cohort activation: Activation programme; targets by end-June; Continue if targets met. Owner: Customer Success
Metrics and governance: Define churn; Monthly guardrail review (p.13). Owner: CFO
Milestones: Dec: decision; June gate: SMB go or no-go; mid-market +12% for the second half?; Oct: 2028 pricing, incl. an answer to Inkwell
The promotion cohort is excluded from any 2027 SMB increase. Renewal notice periods to be confirmed by Legal.

slides.title: Guardrails tell us early whether to pause, extend or stop each move

claims.claim: Mid-market +10%: Monthly logo churn of renewing mid-market accounts
evidence: Today 0.8%; trigger > 1.0% for two months running → Pause rises on remaining renewals; offer a multi-year price lock instead
≤ 0.8% through June → Renew the second half at +12% (+$0.35M)

claims.claim: Enterprise at terms: Renewal outcome of each top account
evidence: Today 0.2% churn; NRR 118%; trigger: Any renewal flagged at risk → Trade the increase for a longer term; never breach the 7% cap

claims.claim: SMB +8% test (June gate): Conversion at +8% vs control; churn of renewal sample vs control; price share of core churners
evidence: Go only if conversion is not significantly lower, sample churn ≤ control + 0.3 pts and price share ≤ 20%
Go: +8% from July for the core base. No-go: hold through 2027 and build a packaging answer to Inkwell for 2028

claims.claim: Promotion-cohort activation: Share sending ≥5 documents a month; cohort monthly churn
evidence: If missed, stop extra spend; plan on ≈45% of the cohort's ARR ($2.0M) leaving within 12 months

claims.claim: Competitive position: SMB win rate where Inkwell is considered
evidence: Today 38%; trigger < 35% → Bring the 2028 SMB packaging review forward

claims.claim: Thresholds are our proposal for leadership to confirm; the pack gives today's values only. Review monthly at the pricing steering meeting.

slides.title: Three open questions could change the plan; each has a built-in test

claims.claim: 1. How price-sensitive is the core SMB base now that Inkwell exists?
evidence: Why open: The only evidence (2023, +8%) predates Inkwell.
What we would do: If the test is clean: +8% from July, and SMB returns to the 2028 plan. If not: hold, and work on packaging rather than list price.

claims.claim: 2. Can the promotion cohort be activated, or will it mostly churn anyway?
evidence: Why open: Activation explains under a third of its excess churn.
What we would do: If targets are missed by June, stop extra spend. Its losses are already in the baseline NRR; a reverting cohort is upside.

claims.claim: 3. Does the 2024 mid-market test (new sign-ups) predict renewals?
evidence: Why open: Existing customers may react differently from new buyers.
What we would do: The guardrail on renewing accounts gives a first read in Q1. Pause if churn exceeds 1.0%; extend to 12% if it holds.

claims.claim: Gaps in the evidence to close before the board meeting
evidence: New-customer ARR plan for 2027: Not in the pack. The downside case needs ≥ $1.1M of it to reach +15%.
Renewal notice periods: Each month of renewals missed costs ≈ $0.36M of the $4.3M.
Board churn metric: “1.4% → 2.3%” cannot be rebuilt from segment data (appendix).

slides.title: Five decisions for the leadership team in December

claims.claim: APPROVE: Mid-market +10% at renewal and enterprise increases at contract terms (7% where capped, 10% target otherwise), effective with January 2027 renewals. (CFO, Sales)
REJECT: The +12% rise on every plan. Hold SMB list prices through June 2027; exclude the promotion cohort from any 2027 increase. (CEO)
APPROVE: The SMB +8% test (February–May) and the June go or no-go gate with the criteria on page 13. (Growth / Product)
FUND: The promotion-cohort activation programme, with targets on activation (≥55%) and cohort churn (≤4.0%), not “halve SMB churn”. (Customer Success)
FIX: The board churn metric: report logo and revenue churn by segment, and confirm the 2027 new-customer ARR plan. (CFO, Sales)
Result: ≈ $98.9M exit ARR (+15%) before new customers, NRR ≈ 115%, and the SMB price decision taken in June on evidence rather than on the 2023 analogue.

evidence: Assumes 2027 repeats the trailing year and that the trailing NRR contains no price rise.

evidence: SMB 21.0 × 12% = 2.52; mid-market 41.0 × 85% × 12% = 4.18; enterprise 9.6 renewing, 60% capped at 7% and 40% at 12% = 0.86
If no renewing contract is capped: 1.15; if all are: 0.67.

claims.claim: SMB churn response: $1.27M; downside doubles it ($2.54M) for Inkwell
evidence: 2023: +8% → +0.5 pts a month for six months, then +0.1 pts. Scaled linearly to 12%: 5.4% extra churn × $23.5M = $1.27M.

claims.claim: Mid-market response (downside only)
evidence: +0.2 pts a month for six months on renewing ARR: $0.46M at 10%, $0.56M at 12%.

claims.claim: Recommended price ARR: total $4.27M
SMB +8% from July: net ≈ $0.40M
evidence: Half of the core SMB ARR ($16.6M) reprices by year-end: 8.3 × 8% = 0.66, less the 2023-style response of 3% × 8.96 = 0.27

claims.claim: Promotion cohort implied churn 4.9%; activation split
evidence: with low senders churning 3× as often, core 2.1% implies 1.35% for activated customers; the cohort's 41% activation implies 2.9%; the rest (2.0 pts) is the discount ending and other factors

claims.claim: Activation value: saves ≈ $0.3M; upside ≈ $1.0M
evidence: 12-month loss on $4.4M at 4.9% a month = 45% ($2.0M); at 4.1% = 39% ($1.7M); saves ≈ $0.3M. At 2.1% = 22% ($1.0M); saves ≈ $1.0M (upside).

normalized.recommendation: Option C, segmented increase: Mid-market +10% at renewal and enterprise increases at contract terms (7% where capped, 10% target otherwise), effective with January 2027 renewals; reject the +12% rise on every plan; hold SMB list prices through June 2027 while a controlled +8% test runs (February–May) with a June go or no-go gate; exclude the promotion cohort from any 2027 increase; fund the promotion-cohort activation programme with targets on activation (≥55%) and cohort churn (≤4.0%), not “halve SMB churn”; fix the board churn metric (report logo and revenue churn by segment) and confirm the 2027 new-customer ARR plan.

alternatives_considered.option: A · CFO plan: +12% on every plan
alternatives_considered.treatment: NOT RECOMMENDED. Net 2027 ARR from price 6.3 / 4.5 (base / downside), not the $10.3M claimed; main risk: SMB deals and promotion-cohort churn; 2027 churn signal becomes hard to read. ≈ $1.6M more 2027 ARR than C on paper in the base case.
NOT RECOMMENDED. Misses the target unless new-customer ARR is ≥ $4.7M; leaves mid-market and enterprise headroom unused. Exit-2027 ARR 94.2 / 94.0.
RECOMMENDED. Meets the 15% growth target with the least exposure in SMB; exit-2027 ARR 98.9 / 97.8; ≈ $1.6M below A in the base case; downside needs ≥ $1.1M of new-customer ARR.

alternatives_considered.option: SMB +12% in January (vs deferring to a July +8% test)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Deferred: buys a measured answer on core SMB price sensitivity, no wider gap vs Inkwell at point of sale, and a clean read on onboarding. In the downside case the January SMB rise nets ≈ $0; deferring it costs at most ≈ $0.85M.

alternatives_considered.option: Mid-market and enterprise at 12% instead of 10%
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not taken in January (+0.77 of the gap): mid-market stays at the tested level. Kept as a spare lever: if mid-market renewals hold through June, renew the second half at +12% (+$0.35M).

alternatives_considered.option: Customer Success claim: halve SMB churn through onboarding
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected as a target: halving needs 1.55%, a rate below anything SMB has recorded; low activation explains under a third of the cohort's excess churn. Set targets on activation and cohort churn instead.
